pairs: Ideoque et nos tantam habentes impositam nubem testium,
Furthermore, since we also have so great a cloud of witnesses over us,
deponentes omne pondus, et circumstans nos peccatum,
let us set aside every burden and sin which may surround us,
per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen:
and advance, through patience, to the struggle offered to us.
aspicientes in auctorem fidei, et consummatorem Jesum,
Let us gaze upon Jesus, as the Author and the completion of our faith,
qui proposito sibi gaudio sustinuit crucem,
who, having joy laid out before him, endured the cross,
atque in dextera sedis Dei sedet.
and who now sits at the right hand of the throne of God.
Recogitate enim eum qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversum semetipsum contradictionem:
So then, meditate upon him who endured such adversity from sinners against himself,
ut ne fatigemini, animis vestris deficientes.
so that you may not become weary, failing in your souls.
Nondum enim usque ad sanguinem restitistis,
For you have not yet resisted unto blood,
And you have forgotten the consolation which speaks to you like sons,
do not be willing to neglect the discipline of the Lord.
neque fatigeris dum ab eo argueris.
And every son whom he accepts,
Tamquam filiis vobis offert se Deus:
God presents you to himself as sons.
whom his father does not correct?
quod si extra disciplinam estis, cujus participes facti sunt omnes:
But if you are without that discipline in which all have become sharers,
Then, too, we have certainly had the fathers of our flesh as instructors,
et reverebamur eos, non multo magis obtemperabimus Patri spirituum,
Should we not obey the Father of spirits all the more,
Et illi quidem in tempore paucorum dierum,
And indeed, for a few days and according to their own wishes,
they instructed us. But he does so to our benefit,
hic autem ad id quod utile est in recipiendo sanctificationem ejus.
so that we may receive his sanctification.
Omnis autem disciplina in præsenti quidem videtur non esse gaudii,
Now every discipline, in the present time, does not seem a gladness,
postea autem fructum pacatissimum exercitatis per eam, reddet justitiæ.
But afterwards, it will repay a most peaceful fruit of justice to those who become trained in it.
lift up your lazy hands and your lax knees,
et gressus rectos facite pedibus vestris:
and straighten the path of your feet, so that no one,
without which no one shall see God.
Be contemplative, lest anyone lack the grace of God,
ne qua radix amaritudinis sursum germinans impediat,
lest any root of bitterness spring up and impede you,
and by it, many might be defiled,
Ne quis fornicator, aut profanus ut Esau:
lest any fornicator or worldly person be like Esau,
qui propter unam escam vendidit primitiva sua:
who, for the sake of one meal, sold his birthright.
when he desired to inherit the benediction,
For he found no place for repentance,
even though he had sought it with tears.
Non enim accessistis ad tractabilem montem,
But you have not drawn near to a tangible mountain,
et tubæ sonum, et vocem verborum,
or the sound of a trumpet, or a voice of words.
Those who had experienced these things excused themselves,
lest the Word be spoken to them.
For they could not bear what was said, and so,
if even a beast would have touched the mountain,
Et ita terribile erat quod videbatur.
And what was seen was so terrible that even Moses said:
But you have drawn near to mount Zion,
and to the city of the living God,
and to the company of many thousands of Angels,
and to the Church of the first-born,
those who have been inscribed in the heavens,
and to God, the judge of all,
and to the spirits of the just made perfect,
and to Jesus, the Mediator of the New Testament,
et sanguinis aspersionem melius loquentem quam Abel.
and to a sprinkling of blood, which speaks better than the blood of Abel.
Be careful not to reject the One who is speaking.
Si enim illi non effugerunt, recusantes eum, qui super terram loquebatur:
For if those who rejected him who was speaking upon the earth were not able to escape,
multo magis nos, qui de cælis loquentem nobis avertimus.
so much more we who might turn away from the One who is speaking to us from heaven.
Then, his voice moved the earth. But now,
et ego movebo non solum terram,
and then I will move, not only the earth,
he declares the transfer of the moveable things of creation,
ut maneant ea quæ sunt immobilia.
so that those things which are immoveable may remain.
Thus, in receiving an immoveable kingdom,
through grace, let us be of service,
by pleasing God with fear and reverence.
Etenim Deus noster ignis consumens est.
For our God is a consuming fire.
